title: Maximize Y‑Sum by Picking a Triplet of Distinct X‑Values
summary: Given arrays x and y of length n, select three distinct indices i, j, and k where x[i] ≠ x[j], x[j] ≠ x[k], and x[k] ≠ x[i].
statement: Given arrays x and y of length n, select three distinct indices i, j, and k where x[i] ≠ x[j], x[j] ≠ x[k], and x[k] ≠ x[i]. The objective is to maximize y[i] + y[j] + y[k]. Return the highest achievable sum if a valid triplet exists; otherwise, return -1.
constraints: x and y have equal length between 3 and 100,000.
Choose three indices whose x values are pairwise distinct.
Maximize the corresponding y sum, or return -1 if fewer than three x values exist.
hints: Only the largest y paired with each distinct x can appear in an optimal triplet.
Aggregate best y per x, then select the three largest group maxima.
Update best[x]=max(best[x],y); if fewer than three keys return -1; otherwise sum the top three.
Replacing any selected index by a larger y from the same x preserves distinctness and improves or maintains the sum.
editorial: Replacing any selected index by a larger y from the same x preserves distinctness and improves or maintains the sum.

tests.explanation: The best y value for x values one, two, and three gives 5+3+6=14.
Only two distinct x values exist, so no valid triplet exists.
